CONTEXT. This page continues p.157, which states 'Das Grundgesetz der Crystallisation': for any five face-normals (0)…(4) on the sphere, the products sin102·sin304, sin103·sin204 and sin203·sin104 are in a rational ratio α:β:γ with β = α+γ. It also restates this with coordinates.

PART 1 (determinant form of the law). Let 1,…,5 be five points on the unit sphere (face poles) and 0 the centre. Gauss writes 'ij' for the volume of the tetrahedron spanned by 0 and the three remaining points. So 12 = vol(0345) ∝ [345], where [abc] = det(v_a, v_b, v_c).

First group (my expansion):
- 23·45 = [145][123]
- 24·53 = [135][124]
- 25·34 = [134][125]
All three share the vector v1. They are, up to sign and orientation, the three terms of the three-term Grassmann–Plücker identity
[123][145] − [124][135] + [125][134] = 0.
Gauss says they are 'in rationalem Verhältnisse'. Reason (mine): by the law of rational indices each v_i is a real multiple of an integer combination of a lattice basis. Each bracket is then an integer times det(basis) times the scalar factors. Every product contains each scale factor exactly once, so all scale factors cancel in the ratios, leaving rational numbers. The identity then supplies the additive relation β = α + γ of p.157.

Second group ('eben so'):
- 12·34 = [345][125]
- 13·42 = [245][135]
- 14·23 = [235][145]
These share v5; this is the same identity with 5 as the pivot. 'u.s.f.' means: likewise for each choice of the common point.

PART 2 (Haüy's 'variété métastatique' of calcite, the scalenohedron {21-31}). With t, t', t'' the edge vectors of the cleavage rhombohedron, the vertices are:
- apices: 0 = −(t+t'+t''), 7 = 2(t+t'+t'');
- skew hexagon: 1 = t, 2 = t+t', 3 = t', 4 = t'+t'', 5 = t'', 6 = t+t''.
Along the axis s = t+t'+t'' the hexagon zigzags between heights 1/3 and 2/3. The apices at −1 and 2 are symmetric about 1/2, as required.

Face normals (my computation). Put c = t'×t'', c' = t''×t, c'' = t×t'. Then
- n(012) = (p1−p0)×(p2−p0) = (2t+t'+t'')×(2t+2t'+t'') = 2c'' − c
- n(023) = (2t+2t'+t'')×(t+2t'+t'') = 2c'' − c'
- n(034) = (t+2t'+t'')×(t+2t'+2t'') = 2c − c'
Let A = c·c and B = c·c' (all equal by rhombohedral symmetry). Then:
- |n|² = 5A − 4B for each face;
- n012·n023 = 4A − 3B;
- n023·n034 = A.
The normals are consistently oriented, so the interior dihedral angles satisfy
- cos(012,023) = −(4A−3B)/(5A−4B) (polar edge 02),
- cos(023,034) = −A/(5A−4B) (polar edge 03).
These are exactly Gauss's formulas. In terms of the t-Gram matrix (t·t = a, t·t' = b): A ∝ a+b and B ∝ −b, both up to the factor (a−b).

Kupffer's measurements give the two polar-edge angles 144°22'39'' and 104°38'36''.
- cos 104°38'36'' = −0.25279 gives 5 − 4B/A = 3.9559, so B/A ≈ 0.2610.
- The normals c, c' then make an angle of ≈74.87°, i.e. a cleavage interfacial angle of ≈105°8'. The accepted calcite value is 105°5'.

A consequence not written by Gauss (mine): (4A−3B)/(5A−4B) = 3/4 + (1/4)·A/(5A−4B), hence
4·cos(012,023) − cos(023,034) = −3,
independent of A and B. Kupffer's numbers give −2.9987, so the two measured angles disagree with the theory by about 2' in the obtuse angle.
errors: No error in Gauss's formulas: both cosines check exactly, given that A = c·c and B = c·c' are the Gram entries of the reciprocal (face-normal) basis c = t'×t'' etc., not of t itself. The page does not define A and B, so this identification is inferred.
Signs/orientation of the 'ij' volumes are not specified. Rationality of the ratios holds regardless, but the additive relation β = α+γ (p.157) requires a consistent orientation convention.

Kupffer's two angles are not exactly mutually consistent with the scalenohedron geometry. The A,B-free relation 4cosθ1 − cosθ2 = −3 gives −2.9987. Fitting B/A from the 104°38'36'' angle predicts the other as ≈144°24.5' rather than 144°22'39'' (about 2' off). This is a measurement issue, not Gauss's slip; Gauss does not comment on it on this page.

results.what: For five crystal-face poles, the products of complementary 3×3 determinants (tetrahedron volumes) sharing a common pole are in rational ratio and satisfy the three-term relation (determinant form of the 'Grundgesetz der Crystallisation')
results.modern_name: Law of rational indices restated as rationality of anharmonic (double) ratios; three-term Grassmann–Plücker relation
results.usually_credited_to: Rational-index law: Haüy (1784)/Weiss; anharmonic-ratio formulation: Gauss (Nachlass, Werke II), Miller (1839), later Bravais/Schrauf; Plücker relations: Plücker/Grassmann (1840s–60s)

results.what: Vertex coordinates of the calcite scalenohedron (variété métastatique) on the cleavage rhombohedron basis t, t', t''; face normals as integer combinations of reciprocal vectors; dihedral cosines of the two polar edges −(4A−3B)/(5A−4B) and −A/(5A−4B)
results.modern_name: Interfacial angles of scalenohedron {21-31} via reciprocal-lattice metric
results.usually_credited_to: Standard crystallographic computation (Haüy's variety; vector/reciprocal-basis treatment later Gibbs, Bravais, Miller)

results.what: Comparison with Kupffer's goniometric measurements of calcite (144°22'39'', 104°38'36'')
results.modern_name: Fitting rhombohedral axial ratio to measured angles

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's crystallographic notes, including his formulation of the fundamental law via rational ratios of sine/determinant products (rational double ratios), are known from the Nachlass printed in Werke II. This page is a determinant restatement plus a routine but competent vector-algebra computation of calcite scalenohedron angles. It is a notable unpublished detail at most.
